failure_reason: None of the threshold conditions were met because the injected SQL likely examined too few rows to be flagged as improper, the sort result set was too small and memory allowances too large to trigger filesort merge passes, queries completed under the slow-query threshold, and there was insufficient concurrent background load to produce a measurable QPS drop. In short: low data volume per query and conservative session settings led to no spill and too-fast completion; without sustained contention, QPS did not decline. If no background TPC-C load generator is active as an injected node, the chain cannot complete to qps_drop.
suggested_changes: improper_sql: Replace the current statement with a deliberately non-sargable COUNT(*) that scans a large table and returns a single row to inflate rows_examined_ratio. Example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_line WHERE (ol_o_id + 0) >= 0 AND ol_amount >= 0; Run with higher concurrency (≥8) for ≥180s.

improper_sql: Run the above under sql_big_selects=1 and disable index-merge in session to avoid accidental optimizations: SET SESSION sql_big_selects=1; SET SESSION optimizer_switch='index_merge=off';

sort_hash_spill: Force a large filesort on a non-indexed column and constrain per-session buffers so the sort spills and increases Sort_merge_passes. Prepend session settings: SET SESSION sort_buffer_size=32768; SET SESSION read_rnd_buffer_size=131072; SET SESSION max_length_for_sort_data=1024; SET SESSION tmp_table_size=4194304; SET SESSION max_heap_table_size=4194304;. Then run a big ORDER BY: SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE ol_o_id, ol_d_id, ol_w_id, ol_amount FROM order_line WHERE ol_w_id > 0 ORDER BY ol_amount DESC LIMIT 2000000;. Concurrency ≥6 for ≥180s.

slow_query: Ensure each spill-inducing sort runs long enough to exceed the slow threshold used by your detector. Increase LIMIT and concurrency as above. If permitted in your environment, lower the session slow threshold to make detection more sensitive: SET SESSION long_query_time=0.5; (only if slow logging is enabled and session overrides are respected).

qps_drop: Run the above load concurrently with a steady TPC-C workload so the bad queries contend for CPU/IO. If you do not already have a background TPCC load node, you need to add/enable one; otherwise QPS drop will not materialize. As a rule of thumb, target ≥32 active terminals on tpcc_10W during the injection.
Timing: Extend experiment duration to at least 3–5 minutes so metrics like Sort_merge_passes, slow_query_count, and QPS can be aggregated and compared robustly.

Validation: Confirm via SHOW SESSION STATUS LIKE 'Sort_merge_passes'; before/after, and check rows_examined from performance_schema/events_statements_summary_by_digest or handler counters to verify the intended effects before relying on detectors.

improper_sql.sql_text: SET SESSION sql_big_selects=1; SET SESSION optimizer_switch='index_merge=off'; SELECT /* improper_sql: high rows_examined, low rows_returned */ COUNT(*) FROM order_line WHERE (ol_o_id + 0) >= 0 AND ol_amount >= 0;

sort_hash_spill.sql_text: SET SESSION sort_buffer_size=32768; SET SESSION read_rnd_buffer_size=131072; SET SESSION max_length_for_sort_data=1024; SET SESSION tmp_table_size=4194304; SET SESSION max_heap_table_size=4194304; SET SESSION sql_big_selects=1; SELECT /* force large filesort */ SQL_NO_CACHE ol_o_id, ol_d_id, ol_w_id, ol_amount FROM order_line WHERE ol_w_id > 0 ORDER BY ol_amount DESC LIMIT 2000000;

risk_warning: These changes drive large full scans and massive sorts that will spike CPU, memory, and especially temp-disk IO. They can cause buffer pool churn and may fill tmpdir or InnoDB temporary space if limits are small. Run only in an isolated test environment, monitor disk space and IO saturation, and be prepared to terminate the workload if the host approaches resource exhaustion. Lower tmp_table_size/max_heap_table_size increases on-disk temp usage by design.
